title: Advanced Docker Administration
subtitle: Engine configuration, contexts, maintenance and upgrades
description: Administer the engine itself: daemon configuration, remote contexts, storage layout, upgrades and routine maintenance.
outcomes: Plan storage, upgrades and maintenance windows

lessons.title: Daemon configuration and storage
lessons.summary: daemon.json, data-root, live-restore, metrics and safe reloads.
objectives: Move the Docker data root safely

sections.title: One configuration file
sections.body: On Linux, the daemon reads `/etc/docker/daemon.json` (or the path in the systemd unit). Changes require a reload or restart; validate first. `live-restore` keeps containers running while the daemon restarts, which reduces the impact of upgrades on workloads that tolerate a brief control-plane gap.

sections.note: Put metrics on loopback unless Prometheus runs on another host and the network is protected.

sections.code:
sudo dockerd --validate --config-file /etc/docker/daemon.json
sudo systemctl reload docker

# Storage usage by category
docker system df -v
du -sh /var/lib/docker/* | sort -h
sections.note: A reload applies supported options; some require a full restart. Check the docs for each key.

sections.title: Changing data-root with containers running
sections.body: Stop the daemon and workloads, move the directory preserving ownership, update the config, then start. Never copy a live store.

lessons.title: Contexts and remote engines
lessons.summary: Switch between local, SSH and remote engines without changing your workflow.

sections.title: A context is a named endpoint
sections.body: A context stores a daemon endpoint, TLS material and metadata. `docker context use` changes the active endpoint for all subsequent commands. SSH contexts are the safest way to reach a remote engine: they use your existing SSH identity and do not expose a TCP port.

sections.code:
docker context ls
docker context create staging --docker "host=ssh://deploy@staging.example.com"
docker context use staging
docker info --format '{{.Name}} {{.ServerVersion}}'
docker ps

docker context use default
DOCKER_CONTEXT=staging docker ps
sections.note: DOCKER_CONTEXT overrides the active context for a single command environment.

sections.title: Contexts are privileged endpoints
sections.body: Switching to a production context and running `docker system prune` is one keystroke from disaster. Use distinct shell prompts and read the context name before destructive commands.

lessons.title: Maintenance, upgrades and rootless
lessons.summary: A routine that keeps an engine healthy across months and versions.
objectives: Upgrade the engine without surprise downtime

sections.title: A maintenance routine
sections.body:
Weekly: inspect disk usage, prune with retention, review daemon logs. Monthly: apply security updates to the engine and base images, verify backups. Quarterly: rehearse restore, review access to the socket and contexts, audit running capabilities.

Upgrade paths matter: read release notes, pin a version in package managers, and test in a staging host. Engine upgrades can change storage drivers, cgroup versions and default behaviours.

sections.code:
# Weekly
docker system df
docker system events --since 24h --filter event=die
journalctl -u docker --since '7 days ago' --no-pager | grep -i error | tail -50

# Controlled cleanup
docker builder prune --keep-storage 10GB
docker image prune -a --filter "until=168h"
docker volume prune

# Version inventory
docker version --format '{{.Server.Version}}'
apt list --installed 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'docker|containerd'
sections.note: Use your distribution’s package manager or Docker’s official repository; do not mix sources.

sections.title: Rootless is a strong default for developer hosts
sections.body: It reduces daemon privilege, but some networking/storage features and privileged ports differ. Validate your workloads before standardising.
